title: Multifocal atrial tachycardia
summary: Several atrial foci take turns. The P waves differ in shape and the rhythm is irregular.
source: Slides 71-72 (irregular narrow-complex tachycardia: multifocal atrial tachycardia)

events.label: First focus
events.caption: A focus in the right atrium fires.
events.ecg: A P wave of one shape.

events.label: Second focus
events.caption: A different focus, in the left atrium, takes over. Other foci join in. The tinted regions are the foci used here.
events.ecg: A P wave of a different shape.

events.label: Third focus
events.caption: A third focus, low in the right atrium, fires.

events.label: Irregular response
events.caption: Each atrial impulse is conducted if the AV node is ready for it, so the ventricular rhythm is irregular.
events.ecg: At least three different P wave shapes, with irregular P-P and R-R intervals.

teaching_points: Multifocal atrial tachycardia: several atrial foci fire, so P waves have at least three shapes and the rhythm is irregular (slides 71-72).
It is one of the irregular narrow-complex tachycardias to tell apart from atrial fibrillation (slide 71).
It is often seen in severe lung disease.
